additional_info.subject: 0369336 - ID0369336-DC/Si-D/TR-[MP / PN 170001131] DC1_StateMonitor_KF13 CRM:00314000120
additional_info.body:
Good afternoon Emre and Yigit,
I am reaching out regarding this ticket
ID0369336
opened for "DC1_StateMonitor_KF13" error flag on charger
pTCY0P
.
Yesterday (22.07.2024) I had a quick call and check with Yigit, to evaluate if to replace the StateMonitor KF14 (on this charger it is installed the KF14 instead of KF13 version), and I evaluated that there is no need to replace it, because:
Yesterday the error flags were not active
"DC1_StateMonitor_KF13" error flag appeared last time only on 17.07.2024
Between 17.07 and 22.07, the charger performed circa #134 successful charging sessions with no "DC1_StateMonitor_KF13" error flags
However, I checked the charger this morning, to start the root-cause analysis of the events before 17.07.2024, and I noticed tat the charger had outlet DC1 OoO. The error flags are the following:
As you can see from the description of the
"DC1_StateMonitor_KF13" error flag, the issue seems to rely in the outgoing coil of DC1.
I checked the logs of 17.07.2024 and of today (23.07.2024), I launched some reboots and forced the converter grouping of the charger, and I noticed the same behavior and issue, which is:
The error is generated by a faulty behavior of contactors
QA21-22
during fastshutdown phase.
"DC2-StateMonitor_KF13" error flag is generated as well. However, the error flag "Outlet_DC2_codes" goes immediately to false, and outlet 2 is available to charge.
From the logs you can see that:
Contactors QA21-22 have to be replaced
From Debug Station, this behavior is noticed also from the fact that the TF1 detects some voltage on DC1 (between 5-10V). The contactors QA21-22 are shown as open  (because the debug station shows the PLC commands and not the coil feedback), but from the logs we can see that most likely the contactors are physically closed. This would explain the presence of voltage detected by TF1, as residual voltage coming from the converters through TF1 connections.
TF1 seems to have no problem, however, on the day of the replacement, I would bring also a spare TF1. The goal is, once replaced the faulty contactors, to verify via debug station if a residual voltage is still detected or not. If not, there is no need to replace TF1. If yes, it might be that TF1 is performing some incorrect measurements, and this could lead to issues.
Available for any further clarifications!
With kind regards,
Fosco Servidei
Siemens AG
